pages.title: Advocacy
pages.heading: Learn. Speak up. Shape what’s next.
pages.description: Learn about policies affecting students and take practical action for strong, equitable public schools.
pages.body:
Montlake families have a powerful opportunity to understand the policies affecting students and advocate for leaders and solutions that help every child thrive.

Questions, ideas, or ready to get involved? Email advocacy@montlakepta.org.

Our advocacy principles

  1. We advocate for evidence-based solutions that enable schools and systems to provide quality education, safe environments, and other resources to enable all students to learn, feel included and thrive.
  2. We believe decisionmakers must provide specific details and plans for both short- and long-term changes well in advance of any choice being made so that impacted communities can effectively digest the breadth of information and collaborate in the implementation of said plans. We believe everyone would benefit from longer term planning spanning 5 to 10 years into the future.
  3. We support fact, research-based and neurodiversity-affirming decisions that enhance, grow and uplift all diverse facets of learning including special education, advanced learning and multilingual opportunities.
  4. We support robust, comprehensive and meaningful after school care that is available to all who need it.
  5. We support minimizing disruption to student learning and existing individual communities.
  6. We support seeking opportunities for gradual change aimed at enhancing equity and diversity across the greater community.
  7. We advocate for better and smarter financial responsibility at the district level as well as better and smarter financial support for schools at the state level.

Learn

  • Rainy Day Recess covers Seattle Public Schools news and policy.
  • Washington State PTA offers advocacy guidance and legislative resources.
  • Seattle Times Education Lab reports on local education.
  • All Together for Seattle Schools shares district and state-funding resources.

Act

Quick actions—sending a message, registering support for a bill, or responding to an alert—can have a real effect when families participate together.

  • Review current WSPTA Action Alerts.
  • Learn about the Billion Dollar Bake Sale campaign.
  • Email our advocacy lead for the highest-impact opportunities right now.

School planning updates

When Montlake PTA becomes aware of new, specific proposals for school closures or consolidations, we will alert families by email and in the newsletter. We will also share opportunities to respond.

For current proposals and action opportunities, sign up for the newsletter or email advocacy@montlakepta.org. Past school-year discussions are not a statement of current district plans.

Each year, Montlake PTA raises funds from our community to support Montlake Elementary.

Staffing is the biggest investment

The school staffing grant typically represents 75–80% of the PTA budget. It helps fund positions or services not fully covered by Seattle Public Schools, such as a specialist teacher, counselor support, playground supervision, or other operational needs.

Beyond staffing

PTA funds also support student programs, community events, supplies, scholarships, and school equipment. Budget decisions are voted on by PTA members.

pages.title: Enrichment
pages.heading: After-school enrichment
pages.description: Register for classes, prepare for the first day, and plan a safe pickup.
pages.body:
View classes and register on 6crickets

Day-of help, absences, or pickup changes: Contact the Enrichment Coordinator at enrichcoordinator@montlakepta.org, or call/text (206) 486-6036 during enrichment hours.

Please do not contact the school office about enrichment arrangements; the program is managed by the Enrichment Team.

For the current session: Check class listings and your registration confirmation for dates, no-class days, fees, and dismissal times. If the next session is not listed, contact the Enrichment Team; do not use a previous session’s dates to plan care.

Learning does not stop when the bell rings. PTA-supported enrichment sparks curiosity, builds friendships across grades, and gives students a safe, inclusive place to learn beyond the classroom.

Register

All enrichment registrations are managed through 6crickets. After registering, you will receive a confirmation email directly from 6crickets.

Before registering:

  • Create or update your student’s profile.
  • Confirm their grade level and dismissal plans.
  • Update allergies, homeroom teacher, and any other relevant notes.
  • Review each class description and schedule.

Costs and financial assistance

Class prices vary by the number of days, provider, and curriculum. Each transaction also includes management fees that help cover the onsite coordinator, financial aid, and other program costs.

We want every student to have access to enrichment. Scholarships are available. For confidential help, contact the school counselor at meguerreroto@seattleschools.org.

Before class

  • Remind your student which class they are attending each day.
  • Review where they should go at school dismissal.
  • Discuss behavior expectations and the Positive Behavior Support Plan (PDF).
  • Pack an extra snack for the short snack break before class.

Getting to class

Teachers and the Enrichment Coordinator help guide transitions. A morning reminder from you helps your student feel prepared.

  1. Go to the Commons area and line up behind the sign for the enrichment class.
  2. Check in with the instructor, who will take attendance.
  3. Follow the instructor to the classroom.

Pickup

Pickup times vary by class and day. Consult your student’s schedule and confirm their dismissal plan before the first class.

  • Parent or caregiver pickup: Students are dismissed from the southeast garden gate. See the campus aerial map (PDF). Be prepared to show identification until instructors recognize you.
  • Independent walkers: Email written permission in advance to the coordinator. Students must leave campus immediately after enrichment.
  • Launch students: Students are escorted directly to Launch aftercare when class ends.
  • Let Grow Play Club: Students transition directly to the club after enrichment.

Late or early pickup

Email pickup changes to the coordinator in advance, or call/text (206) 486-6036 during enrichment hours. Please do not contact the school office about pickup changes.

The published pickup policy sends students who have not been picked up within 10 minutes of class dismissal to Let Grow Play Club; the standard drop-in fee may apply. It requires all students to be picked up by 5:30 PM, with late fees that may increase the longer a student remains onsite. Confirm the current cutoff and fees with the coordinator before your student’s first class.

Absences and cancellations

If your student will miss class

Email the Enrichment Coordinator even if your student is absent from school that day. Students may not skip enrichment unless permission has been received from a parent or caregiver.

If a class is canceled

Have a backup pickup plan in case an instructor is absent and class is canceled. The Enrichment Coordinator will work with the front office to notify families promptly so they can adjust pickup plans.

Policies

Students are expected to follow the same behavior standards as during the school day, respecting themselves, others, and school spaces. Review the Positive Behavior Support Plan (PDF) together before the first class.

Parents and caregivers help the program run smoothly by knowing the class schedule and pickup location, arriving on time or arranging alternate pickup, communicating absences and schedule changes, and helping students arrive ready to participate.

Help

Program, policy, or general questions: enrichment@montlakepta.org.

Absences, pickup changes, and day-of questions: The published program contact is Cindy, Enrichment Coordinator, at enrichcoordinator@montlakepta.org or (206) 486-6036.

Scholarships: The published school counselor contact is Mr. Max at meguerreroto@seattleschools.org.

Staff assignments and session arrangements can change. Use these role-based contacts to confirm current information. The school office does not manage the enrichment program.

The school day

Bell hours

  • 7:55 AM–1:10 PM on Wednesday for early release

See the district’s current bell schedules for updates.

After-school care

Stay connected

Kindergarten resources

First day

For 2026–27, Kindergarten begins Tuesday, September 8, 2026. Students in grades 1–5 begin September 2. Check the district academic calendar for full details.

Meet other incoming families

Email kelsey@montlakepta.org with caregiver and student names to join the incoming-family list. Summer meetups are casual, require no RSVP, and are shared through that list and the newsletter.

Kindergarten Transition

This welcoming, low-pressure program helps incoming students meet peers and teachers, explore the building, and get comfortable at school. The 2026–27 sessions are August 25 and 26, from 9:00 AM–12:00 PM. Register online.

Volunteer at school

All volunteers must be cleared by Seattle Public Schools, which can take several weeks. Start with the SPS volunteer application. For room-parent and classroom opportunities, contact your teacher or volunteer@montlakepta.org.

Accounts and key contacts

  • Report an absence: email montlake.attendance@seattleschools.org and your child’s teacher.
  • Grades and records: use The Source.
  • Meals: manage funds with MySchoolBucks and review Culinary Services.

The PTA provides an after school enrichment program with classes in art, choir, gymnastics, Minecraft, language, writing, and many more. Classes start after school at end by 4:00 pm on Mondays, Tuesdays, Thursdays and Fridays. On Wednesdays, classes end by 3:00 pm. Students may choose to take the Activity Bus after their enrichment classes. The Activity Bus loads at 4:00 pm (3:00 pm Wednesdays). Students must register for the Activity Bus each session.

The After School Enrichment program has three sessions - Fall, Winter and Spring. The Fall Session runs Wednesday, October 9th through Friday, December 20th. The winter and spring sessions follow without any breaks. No enrichment classes are held when school is not in session.

The Activity Bus is available for Launch students to ride. The Activity Bus service starts on Wednesday, September 11th for Launch students.

Registration for the after school classes and the Activity Bus is in 6crickets. Montlake's 6crickets portal shows the class schedule and registration is enabled starting Wednesday, September 11th at noon.

Students who would like a scholarship, please email Ms. Ella erares@seattleschools.org to obtain the code to use during registration checkout.

Registration for the Fall 2024 session will be open Wednesday, September 11th - Wednesday, September 18th.

• Students must register to ride the Activity Bus each session. So, if your student is registered to ride the Activity Bus in the fall session, you will need to register them again for them to continue to ride it in the winter and spring sessions.

• Note: The schedule for the choir classes (for grades 3 - 5) has changed from last year. Choir classes are now held on Thursdays and Fridays. Note that Mr. Mattson must approve those who register for Cloud City Choir. For students who are enrolled only in Montlake Choir, their class is done at 3:15 pm. These students can be picked up at 3:15 pm or they can enroll in the Creativity Club to stay until 4:00 pm to take the Activity Bus.

The Activity Bus

25TH AVE E @ E LOUISA ST (NE corner of Montlake)

blogPosts.title: From Montlake to the Nobel Prize
blogPosts.excerpt: Dr. David Baker wasn’t always the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry recipient. Before the professor [...] was a student at Montlake Elementary.
blogPosts.contentText: Dr. David Baker wasn’t always the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry recipient . Before the professor of biochemistry and his team at the UW Medicine Institute for Protein Design starting building entirely new kinds of proteins, David was a student at Montlake Elementary . “It was just a happy time,” recalls David’s mother Marcia Baker. Marcia and her husband Marshall were both professors at the University of Washington. They bought their home in Montlake in the early 1960s around the time David was born. They have lived in the neighborhood ever since. David started school at Montlake Elementary in 1967. His siblings were students at Montlake and then in the late 1990s and early 2000s David's own children attended the school. “It meant so much to two generations of our family,” says Marcia. David walked to Montlake each day with his neighborhood friends.  In  the 1967-68 school year, David had Mrs. Bain for kindergarten. Then in 1968-69 his teacher was Miss Izuo for first grade.  In  second grade his parents took a sabbatical and moved the family for a year to Russia. In class in a soviet school in Moscow in the early 1970s, Marcia says despite not speaking Russian David still excelled. Marcia remembers the teacher telling the other Russian students, “Why don’t you do it like he [David] does it?” The family returned to Montlake and David went on to play chess and then soccer at the Montlake Community Center. “He was a big reader,” says Marcia.  “I think he enjoyed everything.” David also attended what was at the time Meany Junior High School and then Garfield for High School. Looking back there’s a family legend that may have portended David’s future success in math and science. Marcia says David developed at a different pace when he was younger. She says he didn’t speak much in the years before school started. “Now we think he was just thinking!” At the age of four David told a friend’s dad that “zero is a funny number.” “That story remained in our family for a long time,” says Marcia. The Baker family remembers voting at Montlake School when Washington still had physical polling places. Marcia also remembers volunteering at the school. “They had some unruly kids in fifth grade and they thought wisely that maybe they were bored and so they wanted to give them a little something extra.”  So Marcia, an atmospheric science professor at UW,  volunteered to teach an advanced math group at school. Today  Marcia and Marshall are still in their Montlake home. They still visit Jay’s Dry Cleaners. They still connect with longtime friends and neighbors. They’ve watched closely as the old Montlake building has undergone its massive rebuilding project. Attending Montlake was such a good experience for their family they wish more neighborhood families would do so. “I can’t understand why everyone doesn’t choose that path,” says Marcia. For her son, it was a path that started at Montlake and lead to the Nobel Prize. “I wish everyone would choose it”
blogPosts.bodyHtml:
Dr. David Baker wasn’t always the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry recipient. Before the professor of biochemistry and his team at the UW Medicine Institute for Protein Design starting building entirely new kinds of proteins, David was a student at Montlake Elementary.

“It was just a happy time,” recalls David’s mother Marcia Baker.

Marcia and her husband Marshall were both professors at the University of Washington. They bought their home in Montlake in the early 1960s around the time David was born. They have lived in the neighborhood ever since. David started school at Montlake Elementary in 1967. His siblings were students at Montlake and then in the late 1990s and early 2000s David's own children attended the school.

“It meant so much to two generations of our family,” says Marcia.

David walked to Montlake each day with his neighborhood friends. In the 1967-68 school year, David had Mrs. Bain for kindergarten. Then in 1968-69 his teacher was Miss Izuo for first grade. In second grade his parents took a sabbatical and moved the family for a year to Russia.

In class in a soviet school in Moscow in the early 1970s, Marcia says despite not speaking Russian David still excelled.

Marcia remembers the teacher telling the other Russian students, “Why don’t you do it like he [David] does it?”

The family returned to Montlake and David went on to play chess and then soccer at the Montlake Community Center.

“He was a big reader,” says Marcia. “I think he enjoyed everything.”

David also attended what was at the time Meany Junior High School and then Garfield for High School.

Looking back there’s a family legend that may have portended David’s future success in math and science. Marcia says David developed at a different pace when he was younger. She says he didn’t speak much in the years before school started.

“Now we think he was just thinking!”

At the age of four David told a friend’s dad that “zero is a funny number.”

“That story remained in our family for a long time,” says Marcia.

The Baker family remembers voting at Montlake School when Washington still had physical polling places.

Marcia also remembers volunteering at the school.

“They had some unruly kids in fifth grade and they thought wisely that maybe they were bored and so they wanted to give them a little something extra.” So Marcia, an atmospheric science professor at UW, volunteered to teach an advanced math group at school.

Today Marcia and Marshall are still in their Montlake home. They still visit Jay’s Dry Cleaners. They still connect with longtime friends and neighbors. They’ve watched closely as the old Montlake building has undergone its massive rebuilding project.

Attending Montlake was such a good experience for their family they wish more neighborhood families would do so.

“I can’t understand why everyone doesn’t choose that path,” says Marcia.

For her son, it was a path that started at Montlake and lead to the Nobel Prize.

“I wish everyone would choose it”

It’s a great chance for kids to enjoy a movie, eat pizza, and participate in games while parents and siblings supervise to keep everything safe and smooth.

  • Spread the Word: Share information about Parent Night Out and the Walk-A-Thon with friends and neighbors.

While our spring fundraiser is underway, we wanted to remind our community about different types of donations we accept, and how you can obtain matching giving through your employer.

Montlake PTA accepts donations in several forms. Use the options below to choose what works best for your family. Every gift—any size—supports our students and staff and helps us to keep vital programs like art, music, and academic intervention support available to our students! As a reminder, the current cost per student of our programs is approximately $1500. We know not everyone can give at this level but we appreciate donations of any kind to support our school!

Ways to donate 

  1. Make a recurring donation (monthly or quarterly). Smaller, automatic gifts can be easier to budget for and can add up to a larger annual impact. Our online donation page allows recurring donations by credit card or bank account. 

  2. Use payroll giving (recurring) + employer match. Many employers let you donate directly from your paycheck, often with an automatic company match. In many cases, gifts are sent to the PTA through Benevity with minimal fees. Check your employer’s giving portal or HR team to see if payroll giving is available. 

  3. Request a matching gift (for donations and/or volunteer hours). If your employer offers matching, you may be able to increase the value of your donation at no additional cost. Many companies use Benevity, while others use different systems. Look for Montlake Community School Association, Tax ID (EIN): 91-1117733.  If you need help confirming our nonprofit details for a match, email fundraising@montlakepta.org. 

  4. Give a one-time donation online. Our online donation page includes one-time gifts by credit card or bank withdrawal. 

  5. Donate by check (no processing fees). If your child attends the school, send the check in an envelope marked “Montlake PTA Donation.” You may also mail checks to: Montlake Elementary School PTA, 2025 E Calhoun Street, Seattle, WA 98112. 

Volunteering is another great way to support the school. Some employers also provide grants or matches based on volunteer hours—please check your employer’s program details. 

Employer matching and payroll giving (popular local employers) 

Matching giving is a great way to double your impact! Many companies also match volunteer hours - so please check to see if yours supports either matching giving, or volunteer hours. Some support both! Check with your employer for full details.

Google 

  • How to submit: While connected to the company network, search your company intranet for the most up-to-date matching-gifts link. You can also submit electronically at https://google.benevity.org/user/login. 

  • Deadline: Submit matching-gift requests by January 31 of the year after your donation. 

Microsoft - See detailed submission instructions below!

  • How to submit: Employees/donors can submit matching-gift requests electronically at https://microsoft.benevity.org/user/login. 

  • View full program guidelines (including volunteer hours) 

Amazon 

Program details vary by business group and may change over time. Please check your internal giving portal or HR resources for the current matching and volunteer-grant instructions. 

T-Mobile 

  • How to submit: T-Mobile employees can register matching-gift requests electronically at https://un-carrier.benevity.org/user/login. 

  • View full program guidelines 

Boeing 

  • How to submit: Employees must be logged into the Boeing network to request a gift match at https://boeing.yourcause.com. 

  • For Boeing Total Rewards information, click here. 

Gates Foundation 

  • How to submit: Employees/donors can submit matching-gift requests electronically at https://gatesfoundation.benevity.org/user/login. 

Nordstrom 

  • How to submit: Nordstrom employees can submit a matching gift at https://nordstromcares.benevity.org/user/login. 

We are so grateful for your support in any way. We know not everyone can give, but we appreciate gifts of any kind to our school. Thank you for your support!

  

If you have questions, please reach out to fundraising@montlakepta.org.

Work for a company that offers matching? We're collecting information to share with Montlake families (like the below) on how to submit matching - let us know if you can share more details on your process!

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Calling All Microsoft Families! Double Your Impact for Our School

If you (or your partner, family member, or friend!) work at Microsoft, you can double your donation to our school through Microsoft’s matching program. And there are two easy ways to help:

 

Option 1: Donate directly through Microsoft (fastest!)

  • Use Microsoft’s “Donate Now” option for Montlake Community School Association – Seattle Council PTSA

  • Microsoft matches 100% automatically

  • No extra steps — done!

Option 2: Donate via PTA Auction or other PTA fundraising

  • Donate through the PTA Auction (or another PTA channel)

  • Then submit a “Request a Match” through Microsoft

  • If your donation is over $249, you’ll need to attach your donation receipt when submitting the match request

Option 3: Get paid to volunteer — track your hours!

  • Volunteer your time for PTA events, committees, or school activities

  • Log your volunteer hours in Microsoft’s Volunteer Time program

  • Microsoft donates $25 per volunteer hour to our PTA

  • Your time turns into funding for our school!

 

Every matched donation goes directly toward supporting our students, teachers, and school programs — thank you for making your gift go twice as far!

blogPosts.contentText: FAMILY SURVEY 2026 - results In February 2026, the PTA surveyed families about priorities for the PTA budget. We received 35 responses , representing roughly 15–20% of Montlake families . Among respondents, Arts Programming & Classes emerged as top priority , receiving the most #1 and #2 rankings. Other priorities that received strong support included Academic Intervention , Supplies (such as library books, gym equipment, and classroom materials) , and supporting the resources teachers and staff value most . Other categories such as field trips, science/STEM, and afterschool enrichment showed more evenly distributed rankings , suggesting a range of interests among families. Categories like assemblies and community events generally ranked lower but still received some support. These results represent feedback from a portion of our community and will be one of several inputs considered in PTA and school budget planning . blogPosts.bodyHtml:
FAMILY SURVEY 2026 - results

In February 2026, the PTA surveyed families about priorities for the PTA budget. We received 35 responses, representing roughly 15–20% of Montlake families.

Among respondents, Arts Programming & Classes emerged as top priority, receiving the most #1 and #2 rankings. Other priorities that received strong support included Academic Intervention, Supplies (such as library books, gym equipment, and classroom materials), and supporting the resources teachers and staff value most.

Other categories such as field trips, science/STEM, and afterschool enrichment showed more evenly distributed rankings, suggesting a range of interests among families. Categories like assemblies and community events generally ranked lower but still received some support.

These results represent feedback from a portion of our community and will be one of several inputs considered in PTA and school budget planning.

Thanks to those of you who participated in our survey process! Your feedback and input are appreciated!

blogPosts.contentText:
At the start of each school year, parents and guardians need to fill out forms and pay fees.  Here is the checklist of tasks to do.

1.     Set up Source Account. Parents and guardians of new SPS students:  set up your Source account.  The Source is where you will find important information for your student and links to pay and complete forms. This is also where you will find your student’s quarterly progress reports from their teachers as the year progresses. You will need an active account in the Source to complete the steps below.

 

2.     Note Student ID. Locate your student's ID number by logging in to the Source. Their student ID number is at the top of the page. You will need the student ID number in some of the forms and for lunch payment set up.

 

3.     Change of Address. Have you moved?  Please update your address with the school district.

 

4.     Data Verification.  Complete the data verification form for each student. You can access this form in the Source. Once logged into the Source, click on Data Verification in the menu on the left side of the page.  Please complete this step for each student.  This form is submitted online and must be completed in addition to the forms listed in the next step below. (This is a point of confusion for parents. Only completing the data verification form is not sufficient. You must also complete the list of forms listed in the next step.)

 

5.     Seattle Public Schools Forms.  To access the forms in languages other than English, please visit this site. 

 

New this year:  Forms can be completed digitally.  The links to the English version of the pdf files are below.  You may edit the form and type your name for a signature.  (No need to print the forms and sign with a pen.)  Save the pdf files with an appropriate name for the file (so that Beth can know what it is) and then attach them to an email to Beth at brlee@seattleschools.org.  In the subject line, please list the name of the forms that you have attached.

 

If you would prefer to complete paper forms, please email Beth and request paper forms.  Forms will be sent home with your child.

 

List of required forms to complete. These forms must be completed and emailed to Beth. Everyone must complete these forms.

 

a.    Emergency Information and Student Release Form

b.    FERPA 

c.    Device Agreements:  Please complete one for each student, according to grade.

                                      i.     IPad Agreement for grades K-2

                                     ii.     Laptop Agreement for grades 3-5

 

List of forms to return – if applicable:

 

a.    McKinney Vento Program/Student Housing Questionnaire – return ONLY if you do NOT rent or own your house/apartment.

b.    Survey to Identify Disabled Students ONLY if you think your child has a disability and is NOT currently eligible for Special Education services.

c.    Indian Student Eligibility Certification Form

  

6.     Families in Need Form. All families:  Please complete the Families in Need form.  Answers will be sent to Ms. Ella and kept confidential.

 

7.     School Supply Fee.  Parents and guardians do not need to purchase school supplies.  Instead, pay the $35 per student donation by logging into the Source and clicking on the School Pay link on the left side menu.  Once in School Pay, choose the 2024-2025 School Supply and Online Subscriptions item and pay the $35.

 

8.     SPS Volunteer Application.  If you wish to volunteer in the school building or chaperone field trips, please check your volunteer approval status if you've volunteered in past years or complete an application and background check if you are new to volunteering at Montlake. Go to the SPS volunteer page to check status or to renew or apply.

 

9.     Montlake Volunteer Survey. Our small school relies heavily on volunteers and we hope that all parents and guardians can find a way to help.  There are many ways to volunteer.  Take this Volunteer Survey to learn about volunteer opportunities and to indicate your volunteer interest.  Note:  Completing this survey does not commit you to any volunteer job.  You will be contacted to learn more and decide how much time you can commit.

10.  Sign up for Classroom Parent.  The Classroom Parent app will be used in the coming year to send information, coordinate events, volunteer opportunities, and help families reach each other via the school directory.   We need all families, new and returning, to go to the Classroom Parent sign up page. to be listed in the directory and to use the site.

When prompted, use the

Class codes are listed below:

Class codes:

Beau Browman: 312

Lori Yorde 318

Kari Mills Room 316

Courtney Stump 310

Margaret Johnson 303

Carol Podney 301

Jack Marshall 304

11. Join the PTA.  Join or renew your membership in the PTA. Everyone must renew their membership annually.  To join the PTA for free for any reason, use the coupon code JoinFree.  This coupon code will work for the individual membership option.

12. Subscribe to School Newsletter.  If you are new to Montlake or if you did not receive the school newsletter last year, please subscribe. No need to subscribe if you received the newsletter last year. Please note that by subscribing you will receive the weekly school newsletter AND other important school communications. Please skim the newsletter weekly for important school information. Also note that if you use a gmail address, the newsletter may end up in your promotions tab.

 

13. Payment for School Lunches. SPS has changed their payment system for school lunches to MySchoolBucks.  Create an account and add your student(s).  Any balances from last year should remain in your student’s account.  In addition, you can view menus for school breakfast and lunch with mealviewer.

events.title: Montlake Elementary Spring Auction!
events.summary: Bid NOW to provide critical support to Montlake Elementary Programs. Auction runs March 27 at Noon - April 7 at 10PM.
events.descriptionText:
BID NOW: https://montlakepta.schoolauction.net/2026auction/catalog

Please help your school raise $125K to help us close the education funding gap by bidding on some really great items! This year, we have even MORE amazing items up for grabs that you won't want to miss, including restaurant gift cards, vacation homes, sports tickets and much, much more!

New to our auction? Here are some tips to get you started!

Register (this is a must to participate!) and sign in early so you’re ready to bid when the auction opens.

Turn on SMS notifications to get alerts if you’ve been outbid—don’t miss your chance to jump back in!

Browse the catalog—there’s something for everyone across a wide variety of categories; from restaurants to sports games to birthday parties!

Place your bid and set a max bid so the system can automatically keep you in the running.

Snag Buy-In Parties early—these popular experiences sell out fast!

Stay in the game toward the end—the final hours can get competitive, so don’t wait too long to check back and bid.

As a reminder, the majority of our donations fund the staffing grant at Montlake Elementary. It costs about $1,500 per student annually to sustain these efforts. We understand not everyone can give at that level—every contribution matters and is deeply appreciated.

Here's where donations were allocated for 2025-2026 school year: 

Our amazing Art Program

Academic Intervention support

Office Assistance

Music education

Community events like the Welcome Picnic & Art Walk

Teacher appreciation & classroom supplies

Student scholarships

…and so much more!

events.title: Montlake's First Creative Convergence:  A Literary Celebration!
events.summary: Please join us on January 29th for Montlake Literacy night! RSVP so we can get a count for event needs.
events.descriptionText:
Come to Montlake's First Creative Convergence:  A Literary Celebration!  

 Step into a celebration of creativity, voice and joyful learning, meeting the K-5 Masters in this First-Class evening celebrating literacy! 

See examples of work our Montlake scholars across the grade levels have created in their classrooms.  Read poems they've crafted, stories they've imagined, research pieces on subjects they have studied, and personal reflections!

Explore poster presentations of students sharing "My Favorite Book!"  that honors their imagination, efforts, and the many ways children express themselves as writers (See below for this optional project students do at home with families). 

Discover new worlds students can immerse themselves in at our Book Fair.

Listen to students reflect on their Night Market Projects. Join us for an up-lifting night filled with curiosity, story-telling and overall kid brilliance!  

AN INVITATION!:  We would love to see you there and encourage your student's participation in our first ever "My Favorite Book" presentation.  The link below includes different ideas of what your student can do!  Please feel free to use these ideas as a jumping-off point!   Ideas for poster presentations.docx  If your student chooses to participate, we need their posters by January 26th!

We are asking if students do posters, they be 11x17 inch for uniformity.  Any questions?  Please contact Paula Eisenrich, pceisenrich@seattleschools.org

Please RSVP if you are interested in attending so we can get an accurate estimate for event needs.

We need volunteers to help with this event. Please sign up here!

events.summary:
Dear K – 4th Grade Families,

Looking for a fun night for your kids and a little time off for yourself? We’ve got you covered!

Please join us for Parent Night Out at Montlake Elementary School on Friday, March 20th from 6:30–9:30pm. The cost is $50 per child, and all proceeds go towards supporting our 5th graders’ Islandwood field trip. Only 100 spots available for this fun night!

K–4th graders will be dropped off at school for an evening of fun led by our amazing 5th grade students and 5th grade parents. Our 5th graders have thoughtfully planned the night and are excited to host their younger friends!

Planned activities include:

Movie Night

Beauty Salon

Origami Making

Arts & Crafts Stations

Pizza and snacks

We will also have a quiet space available for students who prefer a calmer environment or would like a break during the evening.

This is a wonderful opportunity for:

Kids to have a blast with older buddies

Parents to enjoy a well-deserved night off

Families to support our 5th graders in a meaningful way

NOTE: Waivers will be sent to you to fill out post sign up. Spots may fill quickly so hurry!

products.name: Mr. Azer's Class Artwork – Raffle Ticket
products.description:
Azer Alps

 

After a delightfully hectic spring, our fourth and fifth graders created a moment of calm through Zen Doodle Mountains—a collaborative landscape filled with intricate patterns, mindful lines, and student-designed details. This one-of-a-kind original artwork brings a peaceful, conversation-starting focal point to any home or office. Take home the mountain they built together.

 

Volunteers: Annie Vithayathil and Jennifer Thuwirat 

Dimensions: 24"x20”

products.name: Mr. B's Class Artwork – Raffle Ticket
products.description:
Montlake Mosaic

 

Created by the students of Mr. B’s Kindergarten class, Montlake Mosaic celebrates the people, places, and natural beauty that make our neighborhood special. Each tile is an individual artist’s interpretation of community—from flowers and trees to homes, animals, and playgrounds. Together, these unique pieces form a colorful portrait of Montlake as seen through the eyes of its youngest residents.

 

Volunteers: Christina Dunlop & Lana Stojcic

products.name: Mr. Marshall's Class Artwork – Raffle Ticket
products.description:
Sierra Marshall Mountains

 

After a delightfully hectic spring, our fourth and fifth graders created a moment of calm through Zen Doodle Mountains—a collaborative landscape filled with intricate patterns, mindful lines, and student-designed details. This one-of-a-kind original artwork  brings a peaceful, conversation-starting focal point to any home or office. Take home the mountain they built together.

products.name: Mrs. Orse's Class Artwork – Raffle Ticket
products.description:
KinderGARDEN

 

Behold the vibrant colors of Mrs. Orse's blooming KinderGARDEN, in all its springtime glory. Our little seedlings melded their artistic and scientific tendencies by pipetting liquid watercolor onto diffusion paper and sprinkling in some acrylics just for fun. Chaos was sewn liberally, and the garden that emerged on canvas can now grace your walls and remind you of the tremendous growth these kids have shown in their first year at Montlake! Please water copiously (with raffle tickets) to keep these flowers bright! 

Volunteers: Ana Torvie 

Dimensions: 15”x30”

products.name: Ms. Martinson's Class Artwork – Raffle Ticket
products.description:
Wildlife of the PNW: A Student Collection

 

Students in Ms. Martinson’s class were asked to draw their favorite Pacific Northwest animals. Their submissions—including drawings of the killer whale, birds, turtles, marmots, frogs, snakes, pigeons, and the wolf—were first hand-drawn in Sharpie, then digitally arranged into this graphic compilation. This artwork represents the diverse wildlife of our area and captures each child’s unique interpretation of these animals. The artwork is in a black metallic frame (not shown).

 

Volunteer: Brianna Home

products.name: Ms. Podney’s Class Artwork – Raffle Ticket
products.description:
We see the same stars (octahedra constellation)

 

We see the same stars (octahedra constellation, 2026) is a sculpture created by students in Ms. Podney’s first-grade class in collaboration with Ben and Gennie Brady. Each panel was created by a student and attached to the frame, which is formed by multiple octahedra. This work highlights what we all share together and asks what connections can be made if we give ourselves the time and space to do so. The artists invite the viewer to take in the individual beauty of each child’s imagination, while reflecting on our shared experience of awe and wonder when gazing up at the stars.

 

Volunteers: Ben & Gennie Brady

products.name: Ms. Stryker's Class Artwork – Raffle Ticket
products.description:
The Run

 

A true celebration of creativity and teamwork, this one-of-a-kind piece was created by the talented artists of Ms. Stryker's class. Each student began by hand-drawing their own salmon. Using elements from every child's artwork, parent volunteer Megan Emslie thoughtfully combined the individual drawings into a single collaborative salmon line drawing. 

 

The class then embarked on an exciting artistic journey through watercolor painting and screen printing. After adding vibrant watercolor backgrounds, the students learned a new printmaking technique and screen-printed the collaborative salmon image over their paintings, bringing the final design to life. 

 

The result is a stunning work of art that captures the spirit, creativity, and teamwork of Ms. Stryker's classroom. More than just a beautiful piece, it represents a memorable exploration of color and printmaking for these young artists.
